trans-caspian-railway.name: Trans-Caspian Railway
trans-caspian-railway.summary: A Russian-built railway following the Silk Road route through western Central Asia, begun in 1879 after Russia's conquest of Khokand, originally to help control the region militarily.

kumis.name: Kumis
kumis.summary: Traditional fermented drink made from mare's milk, central to Turkic and Mongolic peoples of the Central and East Asian steppes, also called airag, with a higher alcohol content than kefir.

tandoor.name: Tandoor
tandoor.summary: Large vase-shaped clay oven, used since antiquity across South Asia, Western Asia, Central Asia and the Horn of Africa to bake flatbreads and roast meat at temperatures up to 480°C.

dungan-people.name: Dungan people
dungan-people.summary: Muslims of Hui origin living in the former Soviet Union, found today mainly in Kazakhstan, Kyrgyzstan and Russia.

nikolai-rozenbakh.name: Nikolai Rozenbakh
nikolai-rozenbakh.summary: Russian general (1836–1901) who served as Governor-General of Russian Turkestan and commander of the Turkestan Military District from 1884 to 1889.

andijan.name: Andijan
andijan.summary: A city in Uzbekistan at the edge of the Fergana Valley, over 2,500 years old and once an important Silk Road stop; birthplace of the first Mughal emperor, Babur.

tandyr-nan.name: Tandyr nan
tandyr-nan.summary: Circular, yeast-leavened Central Asian bread with a crisp golden surface, baked in a vertical clay tandyr oven and often stamped with decorative patterns.

chorba.name: Chorba
chorba.summary: A broad class of stews and rich soups found across North Africa, the Middle East, Turkey, Central Asia and South Asia, sometimes served as a broth or with bread.

pilaf.name: Pilaf
pilaf.summary: A rice or wheat dish cooked in stock with spices and other ingredients, spread widely from the Abbasid Caliphate and known regionally as pilov, polow, pulao or paella.

dastarkh-n.name: Dastarkhan
dastarkh-n.summary: A traditional dining space used across Central and South Asia, originally a tablecloth spread on the ground or floor as a clean surface for food.

fractional-freezing.name: Freeze distillation
fractional-freezing.summary: A process of separating substances by partial freezing, historically used to concentrate alcohol in drinks such as fermented mare's milk.

arkhi.name: Arkhi
arkhi.summary: A Mongolian liquor distilled from fermented milk, adopted from Arab distillation methods around the 13th century and traditionally reserved for family and honored guests.

beshbarmak.name: Beshbarmak
beshbarmak.summary: Traditional Central Asian dish of boiled meat, noodles and onion broth, whose name means "five fingers" for the practice of eating it by hand.

russian-turkestan.name: Russian Turkestan
russian-turkestan.summary: A vast Central Asian region governed by the Russian Empire from 1867, often called a colonial possession, populated mainly by Uzbek, Kazakh, Kyrgyz and Tajik speakers.

krai.name: Krai
krai.summary: Type of administrative territory in Russia and the former Russian Empire, from a word meaning 'border' or 'edge'; historically vast peripheral regions of the state.

avalokite-vara.name: Avalokiteshvara
avalokite-vara.summary: A Bodhisattva associated with great compassion in Buddhism, worshipped across many Asian traditions and known in East Asia as Guanyin or Kannon.

bogd-khanate-of-mongolia.name: Bogd Khanate of Mongolia
bogd-khanate-of-mongolia.summary: A Mongolian state existing 1911 to 1919 and 1921 to 1924, formed after the Qing dynasty's collapse and ruled by the Bogd Khaan, combining religious and political authority.

kangyur.name: Kangyur
kangyur.summary: The collection of Buddha's recorded teachings within the Tibetan Buddhist canon, distinct from the Tengyur commentaries, studied across Tibetan and Mongolian Buddhism.

bukhara.name: Bukhara
bukhara.summary: Ancient Silk Road city in what is now Uzbekistan, a major center of Islamic scholarship and birthplace of Imam Bukhari, later capital of the Emirate of Bukhara until 1920.

chor-minor.name: Chor Minor
chor-minor.summary: A historic gatehouse for a now-destroyed madrasa in Bukhara, Uzbekistan, part of the city's UNESCO World Heritage Site, its name meaning 'four minarets' in Persian.

tetrapylon.name: Tetrapylon
tetrapylon.summary: A rectangular Roman monument with four arched passageways set at right angles, usually built at a crossroads as a form of triumphal arch.

choijin-lama-temple.name: Choijin Lama Temple
choijin-lama-temple.summary: A Buddhist monastery complex in Ulaanbaatar, Mongolia, built between 1904 and 1908, closed under Communist religious repression in 1937 and later reopened as a museum.

maitreya.name: Maitreya
maitreya.summary: Bodhisattva regarded in Buddhism as the future Buddha, prophesied to succeed Gautama Buddha and re-establish his teachings on Earth.

great-game.name: Great Game
great-game.summary: A 19th-century rivalry between the British and Russian empires for influence in Central Asia, especially Afghanistan, Persia and Tibet, fought through diplomacy and expansion rather than direct war.

mikhail-chernyayev.name: Mikhail Chernyayev
mikhail-chernyayev.summary: Russian major general (1828–1898) who, with Konstantin Kaufman and Mikhail Skobelev, directed Russia's conquest of Central Asia under Tsar Alexander II.

tashkent.name: Tashkent
tashkent.summary: Capital and largest city of Uzbekistan, a historic Silk Road crossroads destroyed by Genghis Khan in 1219, later ruled by Kokand before falling to the Russian Empire in 1865.

samarkand.name: Samarkand
samarkand.summary: A major city in southeastern Uzbekistan and one of the oldest continuously inhabited cities in Central Asia, a key Silk Road center once capital of the Achaemenid satrapy of Sogdiana.

khanate-of-kokand.name: Khanate of Kokand
khanate-of-kokand.summary: An early modern Persian- and Turkic-speaking state in Central Asia's Fergana Valley, founded by Uzbek leader Shahrukh Biy as the Khanate of Bukhara declined; its economy relied on irrigated agriculture.

emirate-of-bukhara.name: Emirate of Bukhara
emirate-of-bukhara.summary: An Uzbek monarchy in Central Asia from 1785 to 1920, centered on the cities of Bukhara and Samarkand, ended by the founding of the Bukharan People's Soviet Republic.

khalkha-mongols.name: Khalkha Mongols
khalkha-mongols.summary: The largest subgroup of the Mongols in present-day Mongolia since the 15th century, historically ruled directly by Borjigin khans and making up most of Mongolia's population today.

mikhail-annenkov.name: Mikhail Annenkov
mikhail-annenkov.summary: Russian general, nobleman and engineer (1835–1899) who built the Transcaspian Railway through what is now Turkmenistan, enabling Russia's defeat of the Turkmen at Geok-Tepe in 1881, and played a major role in the 1885 Pendjeh Crisis with Britain.

mikhail-skobelev.name: Mikhail Skobelev
mikhail-skobelev.summary: Russian general (1843–1882) who became famous for conquering Central Asia and for his heroism in the 1877–1878 Russo-Turkish War, earning the nickname 'White General' for his white uniform and horse; Bernard Montgomery later called him the era's ablest commander.

transcaspian-oblast.name: Transcaspian Oblast
transcaspian-oblast.summary: A Russian imperial and early Soviet province east of the Caspian Sea, existing from the late 19th century until 1924 and corresponding roughly to today's Turkmenistan and southwestern Kazakhstan.

merv.name: Merv
merv.summary: A major ancient Iranian city in Central Asia on the Silk Road, settled from the 3rd millennium BC, that at times served as capital of the caliphate and of the Great Seljuk Empire and became a center of Islamic science.

panjdeh-incident.name: Panjdeh Incident
panjdeh-incident.summary: An 1885 armed clash between Russia and Afghanistan over a border fort that triggered a diplomatic crisis with Britain, halting Russian expansion in Central Asia and fixing Afghanistan's northwest border.

vasily-perovsky.name: Vasily Perovsky
vasily-perovsky.summary: A Russian general and statesman who lived from 1794 to 1857.

khiva.name: Khiva
khiva.summary: A roughly 2,500-year-old city in Uzbekistan, former capital of Khwarezmia and the Khanate of Khiva, whose old town Itchan Kala was Central Asia's first UNESCO World Heritage Site.

james-abbott-indian-army-officer.name: James Abbott
james-abbott-indian-army-officer.summary: A British Bengal Army officer and colonial administrator (1807-1896) after whom the Pakistani city of Abbottabad is named.

richmond-shakespear.name: Richmond Shakespear
richmond-shakespear.summary: Indian-born British Indian Army officer (1812–1861) who persuaded the Khan of Khiva to abolish the capture and selling of Russian slaves, likely delaying a Russian conquest of Khiva.

charles-stoddart.name: Charles Stoddart
charles-stoddart.summary: British army officer and diplomat, a noted agent in Central Asia during the 'Great Game'; he was executed in Bukhara in 1842 after being accused of spying.

arthur-conolly.name: Arthur Conolly
arthur-conolly.summary: A British intelligence officer and explorer (1807–1842) who coined the term "The Great Game" for Anglo-Russian rivalry in Central Asia.

yining.name: Yining (Kulja)
yining.summary: City in northwestern Xinjiang, China, also known as Kulja or Kuldja, founded by Erdeni Batur Khong Tayiji of the Dzungar Khanate.

yakub-beg-of-yettishar.name: Yakub Beg
yakub-beg-of-yettishar.summary: Kokandi ruler who founded and led the state of Yettishar in Xinjiang from 1865 until his death in 1877.

korla.name: Korla
korla.summary: Second-largest city in Xinjiang, China, existing since at least the Han dynasty; known for fragrant pears and the nearby Tarim oil fields.

nicholas-ii.name: Nicholas II
nicholas-ii.summary: Last emperor of Russia, reigning from 1894 until his 1917 abdication ended the Romanov dynasty; he and his family were killed in 1918.

dungan-revolt-1862-1877.name: Dungan Revolt
dungan-revolt-1862-1877.summary: 1862–1877 uprising by Muslim Hui people in western China against Qing rule, suppressed by Zuo Zongtang, that caused massive population loss in the region.

konstantin-petrovich-von-kaufmann.name: Konstantin von Kaufman
konstantin-petrovich-von-kaufmann.summary: Russian military engineer (1818–1882) who became the first Governor-General of Russian Turkestan.

dmitry-milyutin.name: Dmitry Milyutin
dmitry-milyutin.summary: Russian military historian and statesman who served as war minister from 1861 to 1881, driving sweeping reforms of the Russian army, and became the last Russian general field marshal in 1898.

royal-geographical-society.name: Royal Geographical Society
royal-geographical-society.summary: A British learned society founded in 1830 to advance geographical science, which absorbed earlier bodies like the African Association and today has 16,000 members.

russian-geographical-society.name: Russian Geographical Society
russian-geographical-society.summary: A learned society based in Saint Petersburg that promotes geography, exploration and nature protection, with research in oceanography, ethnography, ecology and statistics.

tartary.name: Tartary
tartary.summary: A vague blanket term used in European writing and maps from the 13th to 19th centuries for the largely unknown vastness of inner Asia, unconnected to any real state or people.

taras-shevchenko.name: Taras Shevchenko
taras-shevchenko.summary: Ukrainian poet, writer and artist (1814–1861) whose poetry collection Kobzar is considered the foundation of modern Ukrainian literature.

aktau.name: Aktau
aktau.summary: A major port city in southwestern Kazakhstan on the Caspian Sea's eastern shore, on the Mangyshlak Peninsula; from 1964 to 1991 it was named Shevchenko.

asian-affairs.name: Journal of the Central Asian Society
asian-affairs.summary: Academic journal founded in 1914, renamed Journal of the Royal Central Asian Society in 1931, and since 1969 known as Asian Affairs.

royal-society-for-asian-affairs.name: Royal Central Asian Society
royal-society-for-asian-affairs.summary: A London-based learned society founded in 1901 as the Central Asian Society to promote understanding of the region, later renamed and expanded to cover all of Asia.

alexander-von-humboldt.name: Alexander von Humboldt
alexander-von-humboldt.summary: A German polymath, geographer and explorer (1769–1859) who traveled extensively through the Americas from 1799 to 1804 and helped found modern geography.

orenburg.name: Orenburg
orenburg.summary: A Russian city near the Europe-Asia boundary, founded in the 18th century, historically a hub for Kazakh-Russian trade and briefly capital of the Kazakh ASSR.

turkestan.name: Turkestan
turkestan.summary: A historical Central Asian region between the Caspian Sea, Siberia, the Gobi Desert and the Indian subcontinent, mainly Turkic-inhabited, split into former Russian West Turkestan and Chinese East Turkestan.

inner-asia.name: Inner Asia
inner-asia.summary: A term for interior regions including Central Asia and parts of East Asia, European Russia and South Asia, historically covering Manchuria, Mongolia, Tibet and Xinjiang under Qing China.

emirate-of-afghanistan.name: Emirate of Afghanistan
emirate-of-afghanistan.summary: A Central Asian state, emerging from the Durrani Empire under the Barakzai dynasty, covering present-day Afghanistan and nearby areas during the 19th-century contest between Britain and Russia known as the Great Game.

qajar-iran.name: Qajar Iran
qajar-iran.summary: The Iranian state ruled by the Qajar dynasty from 1789 to 1925, founded by Agha Mohammad Khan, which faced major challenges to its sovereignty from Russia and Britain during the Great Game.

khanate-of-khiva.name: Khanate of Khiva
khanate-of-khiva.summary: An Uzbek monarchy centered on the city of Khiva in the Khorezm oasis, ruling from 1511 to 1920 (with a mid-1700s interruption) before becoming a Russian protectorate and later Soviet territory.

borjigin.name: Borjigin
borjigin.summary: A Mongol clan founded in the early 10th century by Bodonchar Munkhag whose senior line supplied Mongolia's ruling princes and formed the Mongols' ruling class into the 20th century.

sart.name: Sart
sart.summary: A historical term for sedentary, Turkic- and Persian-speaking Turks and Tajiks of Central Asia, distinguished from nomadic Kazakhs, Kyrgyz and Turkmen.

xinjiang.name: Xinjiang
xinjiang.summary: An autonomous region in northwestern China at the crossroads of Central and East Asia, historically called Chinese Turkestan, crossed by the Silk Road and home to Uyghurs and other ethnic groups.

treaty-of-saint-petersburg-1881.name: Treaty of Saint Petersburg (1881)
treaty-of-saint-petersburg-1881.summary: 1881 treaty, also called the Treaty of Ili, returning the eastern Ili Basin to China after Russian occupation since 1871.

rudyard-kipling.name: Rudyard Kipling
rudyard-kipling.summary: An English journalist, novelist, poet and short-story writer (1865–1936) born in British India, author of The Jungle Book and Kim, and winner of the 1907 Nobel Prize in Literature.

kim-novel.name: Kim (novel)
kim-novel.summary: An 1901 novel by Rudyard Kipling set against the Great Game, the political rivalry between Russia and Britain in Central Asia; it popularized that term.

maqsud-shah.name: Maqsud Shah
maqsud-shah.summary: Uyghur prince of the Kumul Khanate in China from 1882 to 1930, and the last ruler from the Borjigid dynasty.

kumul-khanate.name: Kumul Khanate
kumul-khanate.summary: Semi-autonomous Turco-Mongol khanate within the Qing dynasty and then the Republic of China, in present-day Hami, Xinjiang, until abolished in 1930; its khans were direct descendants of the Chagatai Khanate.

chinggisids.name: Chinggisids
chinggisids.summary: The descendants of Genghis Khan and his wife Börte, who by tradition were considered the only legitimate rulers of the Mongol Empire and its successor states, a rule that lasted until 1847.

genghis-khan.name: Genghis Khan
genghis-khan.summary: Founder of the Mongol Empire (c. 1162-1227), who united the Mongol tribes and conquered large parts of China and Central Asia.

buryats.name: Buryats
buryats.summary: A Mongol ethnic group native to southeastern Siberia and northern Mongolia, traditionally regarded as the main northern branch of the Mongols and known for nomadic herding.

datsan.name: Datsan
datsan.summary: A Buddhist university monastery in the Tibetan Gelukpa tradition, found across Mongolia, Tibet and Siberia, often teaching both philosophy and medicine.

jadid.name: Jadid movement
jadid.summary: A Turco-Islamic modernist movement in the late 19th- and early 20th-century Russian Empire that promoted Islamic reform, new-method schooling, and print media.

yakuts.name: Yakuts
yakuts.summary: A Turkic ethnic group, also called Sakha, native to North Siberia's Sakha Republic, who speak the Yakut language.

tengrism.name: Tengrism
tengrism.summary: A belief system from the Eurasian steppes based on shamanism and animism and centered on the sky god Tengri, once the state religion of several medieval Turkic and Mongol states.

naqshbandi-order.name: Naqshbandi Order
naqshbandi-order.summary: A major Sufi order within Sunni Islam founded in the 14th century by Baha' al-Din Naqshband, known for strict adherence to Islamic law and silent devotional practices.

ismail-gasprinsky.name: Ismail Gasprinsky
ismail-gasprinsky.summary: A Crimean Tatar intellectual, educator and publisher (1851–1914) who inspired the Jadidist movement for education and cultural reform among Turkic and Islamic communities in the Russian Empire.

mahmud-khoja-behbudiy.name: Mahmud Khoja Behbudiy
mahmud-khoja-behbudiy.summary: Uzbek Jadid activist, writer and journalist (1875-1919) who was a leading public figure in Imperial Russian and Soviet Turkestan.

tamchinsky-datsan.name: Tamchinsky Datsan
tamchinsky-datsan.summary: Buddhist monastery founded in the mid-18th century by Lake Gusinoye in Buryatia, Russia, that became the center of Buddhism in eastern Siberia from 1809.

traditional-tibetan-medicine.name: Tibetan medicine
traditional-tibetan-medicine.summary: A medical system developed in Tibet in the 8th century under King Trisong Detsen, blending local practice with Greek, Persian, Indian, Chinese and Central Asian knowledge; it later spread to Mongolia and beyond.

buryatia.name: Buryatia
buryatia.summary: A republic of Russia in Siberia around Lake Baikal, home to the indigenous Buryats, with its capital at Ulan-Ude.

vasily-bartold.name: Vasily Bartold
vasily-bartold.summary: A Russian orientalist (1869–1930) who specialized in the history of Islam and the Turkic peoples, or Turkology.
